channel.title: Chovy's Blog
channel.description: Tech, agentic coding, and whatever else I'm building. By Anthony "chovy" Ettinger.

item.title: The one task nobody wants to do
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: A Reddit thread asked small business owners which recurring task they would hand off tomorrow. The answer was outreach, and it is the same reason I am building OutreachGraph.

item.title: My left eye is closed for a while
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: A short personal note: a nerve issue has my left eyelid shut for now. Everything is being looked after, and here is what it means for my work in the meantime.

item.title: We hired a security engineer and got back 123 findings
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Eduardo, our new security engineer at Profullstack, audited CoinPay Portal and QryptChat and filed 123 findings across 63 GitHub advisories. Here is what they found, what we fixed, what we deliberately didn't, and the four lessons that generalize.

item.title: Somebody posted my audit writeup to HN, and one comment paid for it
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: My post about 123 security findings went to Hacker News and went nowhere. The one comment it got described a two-week bug-duty rotation, which is the generalization of the thing I paid an auditor to teach me once.

item.title: Going live now — mosh coding at 1:45am
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Streaming a live mosh coding session starting 1:45am Pacific. Join link inside, plus what a session actually looks like and why I stream at this hour.

item.title: HOPE 26 is live from the New Yorker Hotel
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: Hackers On Planet Earth is back in Manhattan for the first time since 2018, and the whole thing is being webcast free. What HOPE is, why the venue matters, and what to watch on day one.

item.title: How to use the moshcode CLI
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: A practical tour of the moshcode CLI: installing it, driving coding engines, keeping agent sessions alive with the herd, logging in at app.moshcode.sh, and claiming a name on the Pit network.

item.title: The machinist didn't get any shares
item.dc:creator: Anthony Ettinger
item.description: I bought LNSR because a former machinist mentioned it in a dentist's waiting room. My own research tool scored it 49.53 and called it overbought. I'm up 30% anyway — and the person who actually made the parts never got a share of it.
